title: Analyses of the mechanism and therapeutic targets of senescence related genes in ischemic stroke with multi-omics approach

evidence_spans.quote: Ischemic stroke (IS) affects 11 million people annually

scope_reviewer.uncertainty_reason: The report labels genes as senescence-associated/aging-related but does not explicitly analyze a senescent state or another aging construct; it also claims multi-omics while explicitly supporting only gene-expression analysis.
scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This is an original biological-data analysis of ischemic stroke. Aging relevance and role are unresolved because senescence appears only as a gene-set modifier, and the generic multi-omics claim does not name a second molecular layer.

causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Senescence-associated gene expression and biomarkers in ischemic stroke

evidence_spans.quote: machine learning-driven Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) identified core genetic signatures
A strong positive correlation (r = 0.72, p < 0.001) between NFE2L2 and PTGS2 expression was observed
PTGS2 emerging as a key biomarker

causal_design_reviewer.concise_rationale: The report applies differential-expression, WGCNA, profiling, and correlation analyses; it does not state an applied intervention, genetic instrument, temporal identification strategy, formal mediation, or directed causal model.

adjudication.outcome: Gene-expression biomarkers and regulatory signatures in ischemic stroke

boundary_cases: Senescence-associated genes are analyzed, but no senescent state or other aging construct is explicitly measured, induced, reversed, or compared.
Generic multi-omics wording accompanies only explicit gene-expression analysis.
adjudication.uncertainty_reason: The abstract does not establish that cellular senescence itself is analyzed and does not name a second currently used molecular omics layer.
adjudication.concise_rationale: This is an original ischemic-stroke data analysis. Its gene-expression, WGCNA, profiling, and correlation analyses are noncausal; aging relevance and multi-omics status remain unresolved from the title and abstract.
